decisive_items: Shows 6 P waves conducting to the ventricle, followed by a period of atrioventricular block.
Prolongation of the His-His interval from the second to third beats results in phase IV block within the His-Purkinje system.
Block initiates after a premature atrial complex and transiently resolves following another premature atrial complex.
response.rationale: The ECG and His-bundle recordings localize the intermittent pause-dependent block to the His-Purkinje system, favoring high-grade AV block over generic AV block; sick sinus syndrome and aortic stenosis do not explain the phase IV His-Purkinje block.

rejected.why: Telemetry pauses could suggest sinus node dysfunction, but the documented AV block and His-Purkinje phase IV block indicate an AV conduction abnormality, not sick sinus syndrome.
Moderate aortic stenosis is an incidental valvular finding and does not account for the intermittent AV block or intracardiac His-Purkinje findings.
